content.title: Walkthroughs: checked, citation-only reviews of a PR stack, behind an experiment
content.intent: This stack adds Walkthroughs: an API-started agent Turn that writes a structured review of a PR stack, where every citation is re-checked against GitHub before it is stored.

chapters.label: The problem
chapters.caption: A summary of an agent-written stack can quote code that does not exist.
chapters.body: A reviewer of an agent-written stack gets the raw diff, which is long, or a model summary, which can invent code. This stack adds Walkthroughs: one guided story whose every claim cites a PR, a file and line range, or a message, and never copies text [1]. Junior re-reads each citation from the provider before it stores the story, so what the reader sees is what the code says.

evidence.note: Contract: cite, never copy; fixed slots per change type

asks: Why not let the model quote code directly?

chapters.label: Starting a Walkthrough
chapters.caption: A click claims one version, and only the winning click queues a hidden generation Turn.
chapters.body: A reviewer clicks Walkthrough on a PR. The API reads the open stack around it and claims a version for that exact set of commits [1]. Only the click that wins the claim starts a hidden web Conversation whose Turn writes the story; if queueing fails, the version fails [2]. A second click on the same commits joins that version instead of starting another [3], and a version still generating after 30 minutes fails on the next click [4].

decisions.claim: The generation sandbox can use the credentials of the person who clicked.
decisions.concern: The Turn runs in a public Conversation.

asks: What if two people click at once?
Is the source Conversation always used?

chapters.label: Reading the stack
chapters.caption: Plugins read the stack, diffs, and files, so core never calls GitHub itself.
chapters.body: Core must not call provider APIs, so plugins get a read-only codeChanges hook group that reads a stack, a diff, or a file [1]. Core picks the plugin by provider and runs it as a system Actor that never prompts anyone [2]. GitHub finds the stack through its Stacks API, or walks base branches until the trunk, a fork, or 10 levels [3][4]. Diffs compare exact base and head commits, so a later push cannot change what the story describes [5].

decisions.claim: Missing a stacked PR whose head is in a fork is acceptable.
decisions.concern: The fallback walk matches parents by owner:branch, so it cannot find fork heads.

asks: Which credentials do these reads use?
What happens when the repo has no Stacks API?

chapters.label: Checking every citation
chapters.caption: submitWalkthrough re-reads every cited fact and rejects the story until each citation resolves.
chapters.body: The model reads the diffs in its sandbox, led by a skill that only generation Turns get [1]. Its submit tool re-reads diffs and files through the plugin hooks, and copies cited messages only after an access check [2][3]. A pure validator returns every problem, such as a citation that does not resolve or a changed hunk that nothing cites, and the model fixes them and submits again [4]. Code excerpts come from the provider diff, never from the model [5], and mechanical files are only counted [6].

decisions.claim: A generation Turn can start without a check of sandbox GitHub access.
decisions.concern: In this generation, gh and git failed with Missing GITHUB_APP_ID.

asks: What if the model cites a file it never read?
What counts as a mechanical file?
Can a citation point outside the diff?

chapters.label: What a generation Turn may do
chapters.caption: Only a generation Turn gets the submit tool, with its own caps and no way to reach people.
chapters.body: A new generation behavior is the only one with submitWalkthrough on, and it turns off agents, the review desk, subscriptions, user customization, and noReply [1][2]. The tool exists only when that behavior and the run's generation field are both set, and only the Turn worker sets the field [3][4]. The same behavior caps a generation at 80 tool calls and $5, and other Turns keep their limits [5][6].

evidence.note: submitWalkthrough is false for every other behavior

decisions.claim: The 80-call and $5 caps are safe defaults.
decisions.concern: No real cost run backs them yet; the PR defers that.

asks: Could a normal chat Turn call submitWalkthrough?
Do the limits change for normal Turns?

chapters.caption: A generation Turn that completes without a Walkthrough fails its version so a retry can start.
chapters.body: The Turn worker looks up the generating version by Conversation id and passes it into the run [1][2]. When the Turn completes, finish() fails the version unless submitWalkthrough already marked it ready [3]. The thrown-error and cancel paths never call finish(), so those versions wait for the 30-minute reaper [4].

evidence.note: Error and cancel paths; no finish() call

decisions.claim: A thrown or stopped generation Turn can wait for a click after 30 minutes to fail.
decisions.concern: The reader waits 30 minutes to learn that the version failed.

asks: What happens to a Turn that yields and resumes?
chapters.label: When a generation fails
Storage and migration
chapters.caption: Each version is a row, one live version per snapshot, and lists hide generation Conversations.
chapters.body: Migration 0100 adds junior_walkthrough_versions with a partial unique index: one live version per provider, repository, and snapshot [1][2]. It only adds a table and indexes. Its one effect on existing reads is a NOT EXISTS probe on generation_conversation_id in every list and search, so generation Conversations stay out of lists [3][4]. To roll back, revert the code first, because the filter needs the table.

decisions.concern: A deleted generation Conversation leaves its version pointing at nothing.

decisions.claim: A synthetic 100k-row measurement of the extra list probe is enough to ship.
decisions.concern: Every list and search pays for the probe, and no real data was measured.

asks: Where does the document itself live?
Does this slow the home list?

chapters.caption: Version status, failure reason, and summed cost show whether generations work.
chapters.body: GET /api/walkthroughs/:id returns status, failure reason, and cost summed from the generation Conversation's cost_usd metric rows, and returns 404 if the source turns private [1][2]. After enabling experimental.walkthroughs, watch ready versus failed rows and their cost; a Turn that ends without a Walkthrough shows as failed [3].

decisions.claim: Version rows are enough to see ready, failed, and timed-out versions.
decisions.concern: No metric or log counts them.

asks: How do we know generations succeed in production?
